Hey, [~accountid:712020:28f7389c-dc34-43f9-b4fc-4a3718af00ff]!

Since Bolt provides platform services rather than transportation services, we, as a platform, should not assume liabilities or face penalties for late arrivals caused by independent drivers. Considering our business model (as mentioned, Bolt is not a transportation service provider), such a clause shall not be included.

An exception could be made by the business if the customer is highly valuable and the contract value is significant. In such a case, the business could decide to include the clause, understanding that these costs would be considered business expenses, and such a clause contradicts our business model. 

Thus, it is up to [~accountid:5f5b4a58c4fbeb0069a85669] to decide whether such an exception should be made. Thank you!

TLDR: there are multiple ways to collect quotas: 

* [https://github.com/danielfm/aws-limits-exporter|https://github.com/danielfm/aws-limits-exporter|smart-link]  goes through Trusted Advisor API, but it doesn't have all services we need
* [https://github.com/emylincon/aws_quota_exporter|https://github.com/emylincon/aws_quota_exporter|smart-link]  - collects only quotas without usage
* [https://github.com/brennerm/aws-quota-checker|https://github.com/brennerm/aws-quota-checker|smart-link]  - collects quotas and usage, but usage is estimated by counting stuff returned from AWS calls. Also pretty limited.
* 

So in the end, we can deploy [https://github.com/emylincon/aws_quota_exporter|https://github.com/emylincon/aws_quota_exporter|smart-link]  with minimal changes to collect quotas and create alerts based on these quotas and values from cloudwatch_exporter data (at least it works for SageMaker invocations).

* Added R703 and R705 for AI UART line protection (AI module burn-down fix) - 120R 0603.
* Populated variant coding resistor R727 10k.

* P702 part number changed to D1-5-3.10 to reflect wiring harness part in the PCB assembly.
* P703 part number changed to D1-5-3.17 to reflect wiring harness part in the PCB assembly.

Panel design:

* Updated Route Tool Path tracks and multi-layer cut-out areas according to updated PCB outline, resolving one source for PCB order EQ problem.
* Added fiducials to panel Bottom Layer as a request from EMS.
* Modified panel break off tab location.

PCB design:

* Changed PCB stack-up definition for clarity of information. No changes to PCB stack-up itself:
** Defined outer layer plating as 18um ENIG - resolves ambiguity issue of whether outer layer copper thickness is base copper or with plating;
** Redefined inner layer thickness as 35um instead of 35.56um - standard copper thickness;
** Renamed inner copper layers from "Layer x" to "Inner Layer x" for sake of clarity
* Added clear marking areas for UL markings and PCB info as text box areas on Bottom Layer silkscreen
* Added silkscreen marking for parameter PartNr in the project name and date marking areas.
* Changed paste layers on Ant200, D301, D302. Ant200 had paste mask openings removed from added pads 1, 2, 3 that are not used for soldering. Paste mask openings were added to D301, D302 pads since the component pads didn't have any paste mask openings defined.
* Modified PCB outline for better potting material flow.
* Moved R512, R515 to bottom layer and away from the edge and mousebite to make producibility better.
* Added silk screen to components P701, P702 to show the component outline. This ensures assembly of components to the correct side of the PCBA.
* Changed PCB silk screen to display the bare PCB material part number according to new part numbering system.

Global:

* Added bare PCB part number and revision parameters "BarePCBPartNr" and "BarePCBRevision" in project parameters and assigned a value to the bare PCB as "MATD-1" and revision "R04" as per part numbering proposal.
* Created rule for CAN lines routing and re-routed CAN lines according to rule

Hey Gabriele,

1.

* Training:
** Simply Contact have been provided with relevant Knowledge Base article: [Authority: Requesting user's data |https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/83887?country=global&language=en]
** Abstract of the procedures for written requests + guidelines for handling police calls are also provided in [Police Guidelines Simply|https://docs.google.com/document/d/11XraaHEH4rca36t9YZdutbq79laMb98AKfP0MtSp4Cc/edit?tab=t.0]
** Per needs - training session with a member of In-house team can also be organized 
* Monitoring:
** All hotline conversations + all cases responded by Simply agents will be escalated to a dedicated shared escalation channel for internal visibility
** Cases replied to by the Supplier will be assessed by the In-house team - if needed, feedback will be provided in the escalation channel
* Escalations process:
** All cases outside Supplier’s remit will simply not be picked up - i.e. if case is not urgent, it won’t be actioned by the Supplier and will be handled by the In-house team during business hours 
** If the outsourced team encounter a case within their remit, but outside their competence (example: difficulty accessing relevant user data requested by the police), they will provide the first reply along with all the information they can share, and escalate the case to the In-house team for further handling 

2.

* Urgency
** Urgency is assessed by the agent reviewing the ticket 
** By default, events within the list above will be identified as urgent unless there is a clear indication that Bolt’s user is only a witness in the investigation and the event took considerably well in the past (like 3 months back)
** The reason for this is that we’re under heavy regulatory and media scrutiny - actioning urgent requests (especially those involving sexual harassment) is part of our safety commitment. Making a judgement call that our user doesn’t seem to be a suspect can be a risky approach in case that person does turn out to be a suspect and it happened during our ride
* Verifying Authenticity and Urgency
** Outsourced agents will follow the same verification rules as outlined in [Authority: Requesting a user's data|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/83887] article (following the part about handling urgent requests) 
** Urgency - agents will use the criteria discussed above
* Urgency is unclear
** If there’s no indication the case is urgent (police don’t provide information about the type of crime, or the crime is not part of the urgent list) - case will wait for resolution by the In-house team
** If there’s uncertainty (for example, police claim that somebody’s life is in danger without providing any information about the type of investigation) - agents will typically take police’s word for it and action the request 
** Either way, agents can also ask follow-up questions to the Authority as there could be edge situations not predicted by the procedures 
* Routing non-urgent cases
** Those cases will simply be left out by the outsourced agents
** In short: agent accesses the ticket → reviews urgency → skips the case (if not urgent) → case is picked up by In-house agents during business hours

h3. *Adjustments on WD to be processed :*

# *Carryover of FRA Annual Leave (CP N-1):*
#* As of this year - 2025, the carryover for FRA Annual Leave/CP N-1 on WD must be set to *0* (as reflected on payslips) and should no longer be unlimited.
#* If there’s a need to carry over unused days, we will handle this manually on WD. Employees will need to request carryovers via their People Partner and Manager.
# *Pro-rata rules for CP & RTT:*
#* *RTT* & *CP N* pro-rata for *starters/leavers,* +*both*+ *daily and hourly based*:
_Monthly acquisition /30 * number of calendar days of employment in the month, then rounded up to 2 decimals_.

+*Update - 22 Jan 2025*+: 
For a reminder of the issues and proposed solutions, please see Michela's one-pager: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/19ezwYSpxvhiFatOYK1PvQtK2tyCgFqXiXfUdpvYZP7g/edit?tab=t.0|https://docs.google.com/document/d/19ezwYSpxvhiFatOYK1PvQtK2tyCgFqXiXfUdpvYZP7g/edit?tab=t.0|smart-link] 

We asked the lawyers of Parallel to give us their legal opinions on the proposed solutions in light of the criticisms raised by the DDPP. 

Here is a screenshot of the +options analysed by the lawyers+: 

!Screenshot 2025-01-22 at 11.44.21.png|width=1675,height=832,alt="Screenshot 2025-01-22 at 11.44.21.png"!

Here is a +summary of their comments+: 

* *Price range* ❌ (options 2, 3 and 4): the price range was criticised by the DDPP as being a misleading practice for the consumer. Price range option not recommended. 
* *Info Icon* ✅ (options 1, 2, 4 and 5): this is a useful addition that provides several levels of information for consumers. The icon brings granularity to the explanation of the category. 
* *Description* ✅ (Option 2 and 3): the description is an advantage for the consumer. Combining the short description on the interface with the long description accessible via the info icon would be ideal.
* *Consumer disappointment*❗:
** (option 1) Without a price indication, the consumer cannot be disappointed. However, the DDPP could criticise the fact that a lack of pricing is a missing element in satisfying the consumer's needs to enter into a contract. 
** (option 5) The mention of a price ‘from/from’ could be misleading because the consumer has no idea how high the price might go. This practice could be deceptive for the consumer.
** The lawyers' recommendation would be to remove the dynamic number and add text, such as “Taximeter”. The reality of making such a product change is not realistic by the end of January.
** The addition of the dash ‘environ = ~’ was also proposed. 



*Conclusion*

→ Ideally, we should: 

* Have a short description on the categories interface that refers to the taximeter (already WIP - [+Traduction EN -> FR short descriptions categories+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_xyOh3tBmwufyUfoDMYO3Uvl-SVTN1FW8GA-7dj_xag/edit?tab=t.0]);
* Have a long description accessible via the info icon;
* For the price, we're going to propose a price range but with an upward markup to reduce possible disappointment for the consumer. 



*Next Steps →* the deadline for these changes to go live is end of January.

Double-checking, will you also be considering cash payments for the category?

Regarding the final payment decisions. I need to highlight that the user debt recovery is *very poor* for debt scenarios, especially with higher amounts. With the keep preauth flow of adding rest of the sums to the user balance as debt means these parts of the payment will not be retried and we don’t actively push to get these captured - these amounts will sit on the user balance as debt until the user returns and places their next order, which may be (and often is) months to years later and essentially they can skip paying the rest of the amounts if they never return to the app altogether as we currently don’t do debt collections. With higher amounts the users also get scared or frightened as the flow is to add the unpaid debt to next order → which if debt of 35€ (_70-35_) gets extra added to a their next ride (e.g. 7€ worth) then the users get an unpleasant experience of having to pre-pay ‘suddenly’ over 40€ for a small trip (and often when returning they don't recall that they had unpaid balance from previously) and it can result in them churning altogether by thinking Bolt has outrageous prices.

In this category scenario, the price changes are significant hence, yes, we would be able to have the security of 35€ but rarely would recover the rest of the sum or the recovery would take ages until when, technically, Bolt has not received rest of the funds and journey is partially unpaid and unaccounted for. This also introduces the problem on liability shift cases - we would not have a definite way to say that user has not paid for this journey as we have not tried to even capture this part of the payment and then as a result we would not be able to effectively protect Bolt and shift liability to driver as we have no concrete payment issue to associate the journey with. 

With release and capture full, there are automatic retries to try and capture the sums that user is owing Bolt and these will happen periodically with exponential timespan so we can say definitely that if there is no successful capture by the pre-defined max attempts or due to permanent card issue then the liability can shift to driver in those worst-of-the-worst cases. It also will then better cover these cases where user may not have the funds available today in case the journey ends up higher than expected but has then next week and they don’t need to open the app and make a new request again for us to receive what’s owed and the attempt to collect happens seamlessly for the user.

There is an option that we can utilize the keep decisions only for cases of small overcharge - so we rather only add cases with couple of euros to debt instead of a full new hour’s charge or more than that.

* *Hybrid system*: Using multiple distance calculation methods depending on the proximity of the courier to the merchant, recognising the strengths and weaknesses of multiple methods and picking the one that suits the situation the best.



* *End-to-End (E2E) Consistency:* The result of a specific distance calculation method from the hybrid system is used across all flows downstream (Assignment, Dispatch, Pricing). The system is difficult to balance when route-distance is used for fee calculation, but assignment is based on flight-distance. 



* *Threshold:* The cutoff point between using route or non-route based distance calculations for pickup. The optimum is dependent on the road network topology of the city, therefore we can consider a threshold that is defined per city.



* *Non-vehicle routing:* Can be flight-distance or pedestrian routing distance. Need to experiment which works the best with the internal map.

HI [~accountid:712020:08485d64-da8c-4826-8ee4-512427d52ff5] ,

* Following article 5 of Lei n.º 68/2019, de 27 de Agosto (Estatuto do Ministério Público), available in the following link [https://www.pgdlisboa.pt/leis/lei_mostra_articulado.php?nid=3119&tabela=leis&so_miolo=,|https://www.pgdlisboa.pt/leis/lei_mostra_articulado.php?nid=3119&tabela=leis&so_miolo=,|smart-link]  “*All public and private entities have the duty to collaborate with the Public Prosecutor's Office, providing documents and information and clarifications requested in a duly justified manner according to the competence to be exercised, within the limits of the law, without prejudice to the applicable secrecy regimes”*
* The Public Prosecutor (Ministério Público) can request identification of users and associated IPs with a determined bank card. The Second Instance Lisbon Court determined in Ac. TRL de 19-06-2014 that the responsibility to obtain the identification of user of an IP address or an IP address number used by a determined individual in a given moment is the responsibility of the Public Prosecutor (Ministério Público).

Therefore, I believe the Public Prosecutor is entitled to request the information and there is legal basis.

# *Found more optimal query (but not fully understand it)*

{noformat}SELECT
  id AS id
FROM
  `check`
WHERE
  created >= DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 169 HOUR) AND created < DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 168 HOUR)
LIMIT 2000{noformat}

Duration 200-400 ms
So, it searches rows for deletion within 1 hour rolling window (instead of fixed 1 week window).
I had to create several such DB jobs to speed-up cleaning and to clean a tail of the tableLikely, following factors impacted performance:

* Much more *narrow time window* reduced number of rows scanned in Index
** However, {{EXPLAIN}} says that it still scans 1-4M rows per each execution
** It *looks like that deleted rows remain in Index* (not physically removed, but just marked as "deleted"). These 1-4M scanned rows correspond to a total number of created rows within 1 hour time window.
* *Rolling window*.
** It leaves many "marked as deleted" rows behind time window specified in WHERE

Some refs from TiDB docs:
[https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable/tidb-best-practices#write|https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/stable/tidb-best-practices#write|smart-link] 

{noformat}After deleting the previous data, lots of deleted flags remain for a short period (then all is cleared by Garbage Collection) and affect the following DELETE statement.{noformat}

{noformat}If too many obsolete MVCC versions exist on TiKV, or if the retention time of historical MVCC data for GC is long, excessive MVCC versions can accumulate. Handling these unnecessary MVCC versions can affect scan performance.{noformat}

MVCC - multi-version concurrency control (stores historical row values to ensure required transaction isolation)

# Include the NJSC release process into the regular bolt-server pipeline by introducing new steps.
## This will enforce bolt-server release during the NJSC release
## You don’t have to merge NJSC to deploy. Hence, you don’t have to revert anything in case of a bad NJSC release. This will improve the time to mitigate.
# After starting a bolt-server pipeline Builder checks for the same branch name in the [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-nodejs-common|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-nodejs-common|smart-link] repo and looks for a relevant PR. If the PR exists, the pipeline is marked as a combined pipeline for releasing bolt-server AND NJSC.
# Introduce new steps for the combined pipeline (before creating the release branch for bolt-server):
## In the NJSC branch, update package.json for NJSC and set the *bugfix* number as pipeline ID
### using pipeline ID, we'll ensure NJSC artefact uniqueness in NPM without external tracking 
## Build and publish NJSC to NPM 
## In the bolt-server *release* branch, set the NJSC package version to the freshly built NJSC
# Merge the NJSC branch after merging the bolt-server branch.
## Make sure the relevant PR is mergeable (is approved)
## Skip merging if the relevant PR isn’t ready (draft PR)

From [Jira tickets|https://taxify.atlassian.net/issues/VULN-42?jql=textfields%20~%20%22mqtt-test.taxify.eu%22] it seems that around 2020 or 2021, the IoT team manually created the server outside of Bolt infra, and someone (probably from SREs) defined the DNS record under {{taxify.eu}} domain.

I couldn’t find any Jira ticket about the configuration.
This server has received multiple security reports in 2021 and 2023.
I see the discussion between the engineer and the security engineer, but I don’t see anywhere the engineer clarifying to the security engineer that this server is hosted *in a personal AWS account* and not Bolt infra!
In 2023, there was a request to SREs about the DNS record and the [SRE engineer specified that he couldn’t find the EC2 in our infra|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/CN6SFK4SW/p1685436940181669?thread_ts=1685436382.194969&cid=CN6SFK4SW].

Many things went wrong here

* No Bolt-related service should be run outside of Bolt infra
* The DNS record should not have been added pointing to an EC2 instance running outside of Bolt infra

Hello [~accountid:5d6cb9744e654c0db0af3b3e] ,
I'll start by saying that managing user accounts is crucial because it accurately maintains trust and enhances security on the platform. Correctly handling necessary actions—such as blocking or unblocking accounts—prevents unauthorized access and protects both the users and the company from potential security risks. Documenting any changes or actions taken ensures transparency and accountability, which is essential for compliance and resolving future disputes. For example, promptly blocking a user's account for security reasons and recording this action accurately helps in effectively managing security incidents. 

When evaluating an agent's ticket, we should ask ourselves this question:
"Did the agent(s) perform all the actions on the user profile in Admin as required by the applicable KB process(es), including adding profile comments?"

If all the required actions on the user account in Admin were performed correctly, including blocking, then we validate this element as "good".

N/A when no actions required on user profile in Admin and no actions done.



This basically involves checking whether:

* the agent issued block incorrectly or failed to unblock the user.
* the agent left incorrect user profile comments or did not leave any. 

But also, if there are Other account actions issues. In other words if the reviewer observed a mistake not categorised.

The latest 5.3 idf release (tested with esp-idf {{fb25eb0}}) does support USB HUB functionality. The modem gets detected behind the HUB. However ESP32S3 host hardware only supports eight channels (pipes). Two pipes are occupied by the HUB and 4 pipes are occupied by each modem CDC device (there are two of them). So practically there are not enough pipes to support modem behind the hub. It is possible however to abandon interrupt endpoint for each CDC device (not used currently anyway) but this would make the total number of occupied pipes equal to 2 + 3 + 3 = 8 leaving no place for extra AI CDC device.

As another option we could also abandon one of the modem CDC devices but this would mean that such modem information as signal strength or selected operator would only be available when PPP is not running. Which could be tolerable I think. In this case AI CDC drivers should also be fine functioning without interrupt endpoint.

Hi [~accountid:610279859798100070592384]the TUPE applies when a new operator wins a tender and takes over services from a previous provider, *provided there is a service provision change and the employees are directly involved in delivering the service*. This means that the employees working for the current provider may transfer to the new provider under TUPE, with their existing employment terms and conditions protected.

However, it's important to note that the Authority does not guarantee that these employees will stay with the new employer after the transfer. Also, of we would want to make them redundant, we would be the ones covering all the costs related to redundancy. 

Additionally, *historical liabilities*, such as outstanding wages, pension rights, or any other employment-related liabilities, will transfer to the new employer under TUPE. This means that the new operator will be responsible for any existing liabilities related to the employees being transferred, even if these arose before the transfer date. 

If you decide to proceed with the tender and potentially take on the transferred employees, we strongly recommend getting strong warranties and proves from the previous operator (employer) that there are no historical liabilities.

Hey team, here is the legal review:

* The possibility of the platform including a category of drivers who speak Portuguese is not currently provided for in any applicable regulation. The current TVDE legal regime does not provide for this option, nor does it require platforms to offer this option to users. 
* Furthermore, unlike taxi drivers, it is not compulsory for TVDE drivers to be fluent in Portuguese or to attend any language courses. There is currently no language requirement for TVDE drivers.
* The creation and implementation of this new category by Bolt +*before any legislation*+ comes into force *is not prohibited*, as we find no legal restrictions in the creation of this category within the current legal framework. 

*RISKS OF IMPLEMENTATION BEFORE ANY LEGISLATION*

* *increase in reclassification risks:* 
** by assuming obligations to classify drivers (qualifying which ones are proficient in Portuguese and which ones are not, albeit on the basis of objective requirements) Bolt is contractually assuming obligations to verify a requirement imposed on drivers and cannot say that this obligation is imposed by law (unlike, for example, what happens with the topic of refusal of services);
** the direct intervention of Bolt in verifying compliance with this requirement may be deemed as the exercise of direction power towards the driver (hence fulfilling a reclassification criteria in Labour Code);
** a mitigation measure would be is minimising Bolt's direct intervention, for example by passing on the obligation to classify drivers on their language skills to the operators (fleets) or alternatively wait for the new legislation to be approved
* *reputational risks:* the fact that there is still no imposing legislation on this option for Portuguese-speaking drivers, and that this is in fact a politically sensitive issue, it means that we can't rule out possible reputational risks for Bolt - because we don't know in which direction the parliamentary and public debate on this issue will go. Therefore, PP and PR teams should be aligned and provide their recommendation on this decision.  

*NEXT STEPS BEFORE ANY IMPLEMENTATION*

* Ensure participation in the category is optional - this is not currently foreseen in the process. I suggest that even if there is automatic access to Portuguese speaking, there is an option to jump out of the category. Would this be possible from a product point of view?

* On 5 September, the driver wrote to Bolt with the following explanation:
** “_Recently, I traveled to Uganda for a family meeting and returned on Monday. During the login process, I was asked to take a selfie for verification, which usually works. However, this time, I received a message stating that my account was suspended for fraudulent activity._”

Hey [~accountid:62e0e5a85b8cc57412052cb6] [~accountid:641aac4c5534b0bf74419b31] I’m not comfortable updating the label on the CS side because it’s a slightly worse experience. Adding “- user decision” doesn’t add any value for users (they know it was their decision) so the label is unnecessarily long and now runs over 3 lines.

I understand the reason for this change is to make it clear for agents whether or not they can “…100% certainly tell the user _You chose this”_ if they request an original payment method refund after choosing BB previously_._ This makes sense from the agent’s & business’s perspective, but is updating our action state indicator our only solution?

If the goal is for *agents* to know if the refund method was the user’s decision, could we instead display a timeline event, internal note or other UI element in the Beehive timeline (and not CS timeline) when a user makes their refund method choice? In Beehive we could have “Yes, I accept the refund to my Bolt balance” and underneath it an internal note, “User decided refund method”.

If the goal is for *users* to know if the refund method was their decision, they’ll know already. They’ll probably remember selecting their refund method, and there’s also a confirmation of their action on the timeline, “Yes, I accept the refund to Bolt balance/Original payment method”. The only confusing scenario I can think of is users who are offered a Bolt balance refund, not a choice, and accept it without realising it’s a Bolt balance refund, and later request an original payment method refund instead. If that’s the problem we’re solving for then we shouldn’t solve this in the action state indicator, but rather in the refund UI itself by making the BB refund method more obvious (see attached).

Regarding cs:

When we refund a rider (e.g., 10 euros) with a Driver at Fault we have the following scenario:

* When we issue a refund of 10 euros to the rider for a driver at fault, the full amount (e.g., 10 euros) is deducted from the driver's account, not 7.50 euros, which was the final amount the driver received after deducting the commission.
In other words, our system does not differentiate between the refunded amount and the commission. We do not have the option to select anything different.
Because if we put 7.5, the rider will not receive the full amount.

Due to this system limitation, which is not able to recognize the different values as a best practice, CS refunds the commission to the driver (e.g., 2.50 euros). However, according to the legal department, this action is not mandatory. Here is the link where we asked about it some time ago: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/4/CCM-18936|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/4/CCM-18936|smart-link]

For the scheme in NL local, this is approx *2K eur monthly overcharge impact.*

!Screenshot 2025-01-23 at 13.44.30.png|width=100%,alt="Screenshot 2025-01-23 at 13.44.30.png"!

*overcharge x dest change x order finish*

{noformat}SELECT 
x.order_country,
CASE WHEN x.minutes_between_change_finish_prompt < 5 AND x.diff_change_time > 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS fast_last_driver_dest_update_and_price_increase,
round(sum(x.partner_price_eur),0) AS sum_final_price_orders,
round(sum(x.predicted),0) AS sum_predicted_orders,
round(sum(x.price_diff_eur),0) AS sum_price_increased,
approx_distinct(x.order_id,0.0041) AS order_cnt,
approx_distinct(x.driver_courier_id,0.0041) AS drivers_cnt
FROM 
(
WITH driver_changes AS 
(
SELECT 
a.id,
a.created,
a.meta.country,
a.meta.city_id,
a.meta.user_id,
json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.data.order_id') AS order_id,
NULLIF(CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.query.corresponding_calculations.user_order_request.input.order.price_prediction')AS double),0) AS price_pred,
NULLIF(CASE WHEN CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.data.price_prediction.price')AS double)IS NULL THEN cast(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.query.corresponding_calculations.user_order_request.input.order.price_prediction')AS double) ELSE CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.data.price_prediction.price')AS double) END,0) AS price_checked_now,
NULLIF((CASE WHEN json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.data.price_prediction.price') IS NULL THEN CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.query.corresponding_calculations.user_order_request.input.order.price_prediction')AS double) ELSE CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.data.price_prediction.price')AS double) END)*1.00 / CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.query.corresponding_calculations.user_order_request.input.order.price_prediction')AS double),0) AS ratio_inc,
row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.data.order_id') AS varchar)||CAST(a.meta.city_id AS varchar) ORDER BY a.created DESC) AS rownumber
FROM archive_analytical.driver_destination_update a
WHERE a.created_hour >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date)
AND a.decision.decision = 'pass'
)
SELECT
date_diff('minute', dc.created, oc.created) AS minutes_between_change_finish_prompt,
json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.order.country') AS order_country,
json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.order.payment_method.type') AS pay_method,
co.partner_price_eur,
dc.price_pred/co.eur_currency_rate AS predicted,
(co.partner_price - dc.price_pred)/co.eur_currency_rate AS price_diff_eur,
(dc.price_checked_now-dc.price_pred)/co.eur_currency_rate AS diff_change_time,
json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.order.order_id') AS order_id,
co.driver_courier_id,
row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.order.order_id') AS varchar)||CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.order.city_id') AS varchar) ORDER BY d.id DESC) AS rownum
FROM glue.archive_analytical.driver_overcharge_check d 
LEFT JOIN ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co ON co.order_id = CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.order.order_id')AS bigint) AND d.meta.user_id = co.user_id AND d.meta.city_id = co.city_id 
	AND co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date)
	AND co.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date)
LEFT JOIN archive_analytical.ridehailing_driver_order_completed_check AS oc ON d.meta.country = oc.meta.country AND d.meta.city_id = oc.meta.city_id AND CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.order.order_id')AS bigint) = CAST(json_extract_scalar(oc.input, '$.data.order_id')AS bigint) 
	AND oc.created_hour >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date)
	AND oc.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date)
LEFT JOIN driver_changes dc ON dc.city_id = d.meta.city_id AND dc.user_id = d.meta.user_id AND dc.order_id = json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.data.order.order_id')
WHERE d.created_hour >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date)
AND d.meta.country = 'nl'
AND co.payment_method_group = 'in-app'
AND dc.rownumber = 1
) AS x 
WHERE x.rownum = 1
GROUP BY 1,2{noformat}

{code:sql}SELECT
date(date_trunc('month',x.created)) AS month,
--x.user_payments__chargeback_payments,
--x.payment_method_type,
--x.country_code,
--x.decision,
APPROX_DISTINCT(x.id,0.0041) AS count_orders,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.partner_price_eur) AS double),2) AS inapp_gmv_eur,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.user_price_eur) AS double),2) AS user_price_sum_eur,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN x.is_payment_problem THEN x.id END,0.0041) AS count_pp,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN x.is_payment_problem THEN x.id END,0.0041)*1.0000/NULLIF(APPROX_DISTINCT(x.id,0.0041),0) AS double),4),0) AS ratio_pp,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.is_payment_problem THEN x.potential_fraud_loss_eur END) AS double),2),0) AS pp_sum_eur,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.is_payment_problem THEN x.potential_fraud_loss_eur END) AS double),2),0)*1.0000/NULLIF(SUM(x.user_price_eur),0) AS double),4),0) AS pp_sum_ratio,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN x.propagated_chargeback THEN x.id END,0.0041) AS count_propagated,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN x.propagated_chargeback THEN x.id END,0.0041)*1.0000/NULLIF(APPROX_DISTINCT(x.id,0.0041),0) AS double),4),0) AS ratio_propagated,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.propagated_chargeback THEN x.card_captured_eur END) AS double),2),0) AS propagated_sum_eur,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.propagated_chargeback THEN x.card_captured_eur END) AS double),2),0)*1.0000/NULLIF(SUM(x.user_price_eur),0) AS double),4),0) AS propagated_sum_ratio,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN x.is_chargeback OR x.is_payment_problem OR x.propagated_chargeback THEN x.id END,0.0041) AS count_fraud,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN x.is_chargeback OR x.is_payment_problem OR x.propagated_chargeback THEN x.id END,0.0041)*1.0000/NULLIF(APPROX_DISTINCT(x.id,0.0041),0) AS double),4),0) AS ratio_fraud,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.propagated_chargeback THEN x.card_captured_eur WHEN x.is_chargeback THEN x.chargeback_amount_eur WHEN x.is_payment_problem THEN x.potential_fraud_loss_eur ELSE 0 END) AS double),2),0) AS fraud_sum_eur,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.propagated_chargeback THEN x.card_captured_eur WHEN x.is_chargeback THEN x.chargeback_amount_eur WHEN x.is_payment_problem THEN x.potential_fraud_loss_eur ELSE 0 END) AS double),2),0)*1.0000/NULLIF(SUM(x.user_price_eur),0) AS double),4),0) AS fraud_sum_ratio,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.potential_fraud_loss_eur) AS double),2) AS potential_fraud_loss_eur,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.reporting_fraud_loss_eur) AS double),2) AS reporting_fraud_loss_eur
FROM (
SELECT DISTINCT 
etl.id,
etl.created,
etl.payment_method_type,
etl.country_code,
etl.card_captured_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate AS card_captured_eur,
etl.chargeback_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate AS chargeback_amount_eur,
etl.uncovered_amount*1.00/etl.eur_currency_rate AS uncovered_eur,
etl.initial_failed_payment_amount*1.00/etl.eur_currency_rate AS initial_failed_eur,
etl.potential_fraud_loss_eur,
etl.reporting_fraud_loss_eur,
etl.is_initial_failed_payment,
etl.is_final_failed_payment,
etl.is_chargeback,
etl.is_payment_problem,
etl.propagated_chargeback,
etl.partner_price_eur,
etl.user_price_eur
FROM archive_analytical.user_top_up_request a
LEFT JOIN ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders etl ON etl.order_id = a.meta.order_id AND etl.order_type = 'top_up' AND etl.created_date >= date '2024-09-01'
WHERE a.created_hour >= date '2024-09-01'
AND (json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.additional.card.challenge.payment.days_since_liability_shift_with_friction') IS NOT NULL 
OR json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.additional.card.challenge.add_card.liability_shift') = 'with_friction')
--AND json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.additional.card.challenge.add_card.liability_shift') = 'with_friction'
AND a.decision.decision = 'CHALLENGE'
) AS x
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 DESC {code}

APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN x.propagated_chargeback THEN x.id END,0.0041) AS count_propagated,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN x.propagated_chargeback THEN x.id END,0.0041)*1.0000/NULLIF(APPROX_DISTINCT(x.id,0.0041),0) AS double),4),0) AS ratio_propagated,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.propagated_chargeback THEN x.card_captured_eur END) AS double),2),0) AS propagated_sum_eur,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.propagated_chargeback THEN x.card_captured_eur END) AS double),2),0)*1.0000/NULLIF(SUM(x.user_price_eur),0) AS double),4),0) AS propagated_sum_ratio,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN x.is_chargeback OR x.is_payment_problem OR x.propagated_chargeback THEN x.id END,0.0041) AS count_fraud,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN x.is_chargeback OR x.is_payment_problem OR x.propagated_chargeback THEN x.id END,0.0041)*1.0000/NULLIF(APPROX_DISTINCT(x.id,0.0041),0) AS double),4),0) AS ratio_fraud,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.propagated_chargeback THEN x.card_captured_eur WHEN x.is_chargeback THEN x.chargeback_amount_eur WHEN x.is_payment_problem THEN x.potential_fraud_loss_eur ELSE 0 END) AS double),2),0) AS fraud_sum_eur,
COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(COALESCE(ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN x.propagated_chargeback THEN x.card_captured_eur WHEN x.is_chargeback THEN x.chargeback_amount_eur WHEN x.is_payment_problem THEN x.potential_fraud_loss_eur ELSE 0 END) AS double),2),0)*1.0000/NULLIF(SUM(x.user_price_eur),0) AS double),4),0) AS fraud_sum_ratio,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.potential_fraud_loss_eur) AS double),2) AS potential_fraud_loss_eur,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.reporting_fraud_loss_eur) AS double),2) AS reporting_fraud_loss_eur
FROM (
SELECT DISTINCT 
etl.id,
etl.created,
etl.payment_method_type,
etl.country_code,
etl.card_captured_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate AS card_captured_eur,
etl.chargeback_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate AS chargeback_amount_eur,
etl.uncovered_amount*1.00/etl.eur_currency_rate AS uncovered_eur,
etl.initial_failed_payment_amount*1.00/etl.eur_currency_rate AS initial_failed_eur,
etl.potential_fraud_loss_eur,
etl.reporting_fraud_loss_eur,
etl.is_initial_failed_payment,
etl.is_final_failed_payment,
etl.is_chargeback,
etl.is_payment_problem,
etl.propagated_chargeback,
etl.partner_price_eur,
etl.user_price_eur
FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl 
JOIN users u ON etl.user_id = u.user_id AND u.ROW_NUMBER_desc = 1 
WHERE etl.created_date >= date '2024-10-01'	 
AND etl.order_type = 'rides'
AND etl.order_state = 'finished' 	
AND etl.payment_method_group IN ('in-app','bolt_credit')
AND etl.payment_method_type IN ('card','processout')
AND etl.payment_method_type <> 'business'
AND etl.created < u.created
AND etl.uncovered_amount > 0 
AND u.top_up_local >= etl.uncovered_amount
) AS x
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 DESC {code}

The user is reporting a double-charge because of incremental authorization.
Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. This typically happens in scenarios where the final amount of the transaction is not known upfront or may change.

I have checked the case and everything looks good on Bolt’s end. The pre-authorization has been released to the customer.

_Part 1 of my EDA:_

I looked at the available data for airport regions. Unlike admin, the regions in {{ng_public_spark.admin_system_region}} are not tagged with identifiers whether they are airports or not. To overcome this I linked the region name using the orders, and the table {{core_models_spark.dim_airport}} where approximately 130+ airports are stored. 

Looking at the matched data we notice several things. 

* While the most common connection is airport->non-airport or non-airport->airport, there are also cases where orders connect airport->same-airport and airport->different-airport (both intra-city, ie. Paris Orly to Paris CDG; as well as inter-city, ie. Amsterdam Schiphol to Düsseldorf).
* Not all orders originating from an airport and marked as such in {{core_models_spark.fact_rides_order}} have the same region assigned to them. (ie. orders originating from Amsterdam Schiphol Airport mostly have the region “Schiphol Airport” but a small number use “Amsterdam Greater Area” as the region).
* Region naming is inconsistent, sometimes it is named after the airport, sometimes it is named after the city, sometimes it is just named “airport”. Considering all this, the pickup_airport and destination_airport fields are much more solid identifiers of orders related to airport than regions. This is relevant for further analysis on categories and metrics. 
* A simple cleaning of the data can be done by only considering orders that originate from an airport and have a destination airport of “null”. These represent the bulk or orders relevant to orders _from_ an airport, and will filter out currently unknown or not fully understand edge cases. 

{noformat}%sql
SELECT b.name AS region_name
, order_city_id
, pickup_airport_id
, destination_airport_id
, c.airport_name AS pickup_airport
, d.airport_name AS destrination_airport
, COUNT(1)
, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.order_state = 'finished' THEN a.order_key END) AS finished_orders
FROM core_models_spark.fact_rides_order a
  LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.admin_system_region b 
    ON a.region_id = b.id
  LEFT JOIN core_models_spark.dim_airport c
    ON a.pickup_airport_id = c.airport_id
  LEFT JOIN core_models_spark.dim_airport d
    ON a.destination_airport_id = d.airport_id
WHERE (pickup_airport_id IS NOT NULL OR destination_airport_id IS NOT NULL)
AND a.created_date >= '2025-01-01'
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6
LIMIT 1000{noformat}

We have different processes for in-app and cash rides because the *in-app cancellation fee is added automatically by the system*, and the *cash cancellation fee is compensated manually*.

For in-app rides, agents don’t need to take any manual action to double-check what the system has already done when adding or not adding the cancellation fee. For cash payments, since the cancellation fee is added manually by agents or Alfred, we have a different process, and agents need to check the driver’s eligibility for the fee.

Additionally, while reviewing this process for your request, I noticed that the in-app payment process didn’t include a section for cases where the cancellation fee was *refunded* to the rider. I’ve added this section and shared the update with agents.

** To add: If you have multiple *promotions of the same type* *active simultaneously*, the promotion with *the higher discount will take priority* and be available to order. 
 
For example, if you set a 40% new eater promotion and a 20% entire menu discount for the same dates, new customers will only see the 40% discount on their purchase, while returning users will get the 20% entire menu offer.
 
Also, note that free delivery promotions are applied independently of entire menu discounts. This means it is possible to run free delivery promotions and menu discounts at the same time, as these are different types of promotions!

Hi, 
I want to make this super clear. If we were to proceed with only keep pre-booking decisions then we will create a lot of debt that will be a bad experience for the user, cause significant delays for Bolt to capture the remaining amounts and we can’t say an unpaid amount is problematic in the end as we have never tried to get it.

Please revisit the scenarios for each option:

*Option 1*: We keep the pre-authorised amount and add rest to user balance as debt. This is bad flow for larger sums as the balance sits inactive and Bolt does not make attempts to charge the customer for this amount - it remains there on user balance and needs to only be paid before or with the next trip. Balance debt does not have payment tries or recurring reminders for user to pay.

Real-life example to illustrate option 1: total journey price is 70€, we keep the first 35€ and add the debt of 35€ to user balance. The user does not make any other trips for 5 months and the debt remains on their balance. After the long time off, user starts ordering a regular journey (worth 6€) and gets displayed a payment amount of 41€ in order to place their order. As we have not tried to capture the remaining unpaid amounts from the user in this 5 months, we can’t apply driver liability in cases of fraud.

*Option 2*  - We still do the pre-booking to check the user but we release the pre-booked amount and attempt to get the full amount altogether. This option also keeps re-trying to capture in any case the user has had a payment problem and the user has one payment instead of splits. The risk here is that we let the pre-booked amount go. We can also say that we have tried to capture the user for the full trip and say that the payment is problematic (or not) in order to apply driver liability and save Bolt from irregular activity. 

*Option 3* - [mixed] - We keep pre-booking only for cases where the price increase(from pre-booking) is small, as an example, due to additional tolls from alternative route taken or small additional charge due to added tips. So in case the trip ends in 40€, we keep the 35€ and add 5€ on user balance as debt. And for the high priced journeys such as 70€ we attempt to make a full payment charge instead.

*I am available for a meeting/call in case you’d like to get further details, discuss in person or have further questions on this.*

I already raised an issue to the Basket Product Team and Director of Product regarding the *privacy requirements for pharma delivery in all Food locations*, however, I need to raise it here as well and inform that *we STRONGLY DO NOT RECOMMEND launching the delivery from pharmacies until we implement/consider the risk below*:
{panel}

*Issue:* On Oct 4, 2024, the Court of Justice of the EU (CJEU) made a decision regarding processing and selling of medical products from pharmacies on online platforms like Amazon or marketplaces like Bolt , Glovo and Wolt. In short, the Court states that selling such products constitutes *processing of health data* even if it's non-prescription medicine and *requires explicit consent of the customer for processing such data BEFORE these products are placed in the basket and sold.*



*Analysis:* Of course, this was considered before and there were only vague decisions of data protection authorities regarding *processing this data for delivering orders*. However, this decision of the Court completely changes the game now in this regard and states that *the collection of the name, delivery address and medical items sold* is capable of revealing information regarding health status of a person. Even if we are not going to analyse this, *the Court still confirms this is special categories of data and processing this data even for delivering an order requires explicit consent of the user.Note:* This concerns only deliveries from pharmacies and not grocery stores that sell some medical products



*Competitors:* I checked Amazon Pharmacy, Glovo and Wolt pharmacies delivery and no one of them asks any explicit consent from users or makes any notification regarding this.



*What we need to do:* To be honest, I tried to think how we can make it painless for Bolt and do not see how we can implement this consent into the basket without slightly ruining the orders amount (). Ideally, it should look like:

* User wants to add medical products to the basket -> We ask the user to confirm that the user agrees that Bolt will process the data that constitutes health data in accordance with our Privacy Notice -> user agrees -> we process the order.
* If user disagrees -> we inform that the delivery cannot be made as the consent is not received.

From my pov, this requirement and decision completely ruins the delivery process for all companies like Bolt. However, I have to address this risk to you for consideration.



*Risk:* *HIGH.* If the consent is not implemented, this will constitute illegal processing of special categories of data. AKI (Estonian data protection authority) will request to shut down or stop the delivery without consent, request to implement consent and delete all data related to such orders. Bad scenario (we do not anticipate this), to shut down deliveries from pharmacies and fine up to 500k euro or 1 million depending on the user number, locations and time the data has been processed.

*Probability:* LOW-MEDIUM. The chance that we will face this request in the near future is a bit LOW as this is not a popular topic at all and there were no any decisions (except 1 in Netherlands and this one by the CJEU). However, as this CJEU decision is fresh (end of 2024) and Bolt is launching pharmacies, we can anticipate some review by the authorities, so the probability is MEDIUM.

[~accountid:5ff4436491bb2e0108d1548d] you asked for alternative solutions to completely split “action state indicator”(bubble with refund details) translations into separate webview and Beehive parts. I’ll list them below with estimates:


# Add a “flag” to {{AgentActionStateMessageRenderer}} in {{customer-support}}service - interface is shared for all actions (so flag would be added for account_deletion/refunds/free_delivery_token etc. This flag would indicate whenever “refund destination was picked by the user”.  Webview can simply ignore it, we can add custom renderedrin Beehive to add “user decision” somewhere in the message bubble whenever “user_decision” flag is true and “action_type” is Bolt Balance or Original Payment method.
## Pros:
### fastest one (probably 1 day for BE + FE)
## Cons
### We’re adding patches on top of already “patched” approaches. Adding flag to generic interface will bring up some maintenance questions in the future (ex: “How should we handle this flag in the context of account deletion action?”
# Updating {{AgentActionStateMessageRenderer}} to return “actual” action_type (which is delivery_refund or ridehailing_refund) and then either split generic interface and apply “strategy pattern” based on action type and/or simply add “subtype” (which would tell what was the destination selected by the user - if user already selected it),  implement new renders for this action_type on Webview and Beehive (icons and some styling).
## Pros
### Imo good compromise (effort vs maintainability) between hacking it with a flag and completely splitting translations for “action state indicator”
## Cons
### a bit more effort than 1: (I’d say 0.5d for backend, 0.5d for WebView and 0.5d for Beehive Frontend)

Hey team, here is the legal review:

* The possibility of the platform including a category of drivers who speak Portuguese is not currently provided for in any applicable regulation. The current TVDE legal regime does not provide for this option, nor does it require platforms to offer this option to users.
* Furthermore, unlike taxi drivers, it is not compulsory for TVDE drivers to be fluent in Portuguese or to attend any language courses. There is currently no language requirement for TVDE drivers.
* The creation and implementation of this new category by Bolt +*before any legislation*+ comes into force *is not prohibited*, as we find no legal restrictions in the creation of this category within the current legal framework.

*RISKS OF IMPLEMENTATION BEFORE ANY LEGISLATION*

* *increase in reclassification risks:*
** by assuming obligations to classify drivers (qualifying which ones are proficient in Portuguese and which ones are not, albeit on the basis of objective requirements) Bolt is contractually assuming obligations to verify a requirement imposed on drivers and cannot say that this obligation is imposed by law (unlike, for example, what happens with the topic of refusal of services);
** the direct intervention of Bolt in verifying compliance with this requirement may be deemed as the exercise of direction power towards the driver (hence fulfilling a reclassification criteria in Labour Code);
** a mitigation measure would be is minimising Bolt's direct intervention, for example by passing on the obligation to classify drivers on their language skills to the operators (fleets) or alternatively wait for the new legislation to be approved
* *reputational risks:* the fact that there is still no imposing legislation on this option for Portuguese-speaking drivers, and that this is in fact a politically sensitive issue, it means that we can't rule out possible reputational risks for Bolt - because we don't know in which direction the parliamentary and public debate on this issue will go. Therefore, PP and PR teams should be aligned and provide their recommendation on this decision.  [~accountid:712020:011a9eb3-77af-4c62-bb26-e6c10e6097ec] and [~accountid:60ec731b2f97d50069db1627] cc’d

*NEXT STEPS BEFORE ANY IMPLEMENTATION*

* Ensure participation in the category is optional - this is not currently foreseen in the process. I suggest that even if there is automatic access to Portuguese speaking, there is an option to jump out of the category. Would this be possible from a product point of view?
* Ensure review by privacy team [~accountid:712020:a7a7d4bc-10ca-44a0-a22e-fa8752330abd] cc’d
* Update t&c for TVDE operators and passengers:
** inform both operators and passengers that the new category is merely optional+;+
** clarify that any wording in the t&c do not explicitly limit or exclude those who are not “Portuguese”, but rather to classify the drivers as regards language proficiency in benefit of the quality of services provided to the user.
* Review all information in app, communications and website to ensure it does not explicitly limit or exclude those who are not “Portuguese”, but rather to classify the drivers as regards language proficiency in benefit of the quality of services provided to the user.
* Monitor the category deployment in to understand the impact on all drivers, particularly with regard to possible discrimination issues, and on users.

Este serviço de transporte é fornecido por um operador de táxi, o qual é uma entidade independente da Bolt. O preço apresentado na app constitui um intervalo de preço estimado com base na legislação aplicável. Este intervalo de preço é fornecido apenas a título indicativo e não é vinculativo nem para o operador de táxi nem para a Bolt. O preço final poderá não corresponder à estimativa, uma vez que será determinado pelo taxímetro em função da distância percorrida, dos tempos de espera, suplementos e outras circunstâncias efetivas do serviço. O preço final será o indicado no taxímetro uma vez concluída a viagem, sendo o mesmo comunicado pelo operador de táxi na Plataforma Bolt. O tarifário em vigor encontra-se disponível para consulta pelo passageiro no veículo.

ENGLISH VERSION
This transport service is provided by a taxi operator, which is an independent entity from Bolt. The price shown in the app is an estimated price range based on the applicable legislation. This price range is provided for guidance only and is not binding on either the taxi operator or Bolt. The final price may not correspond to the estimate, as it will be determined by the taximeter depending on the distance travelled, waiting times, supplements and other actual circumstances of the service. The final price will be the one shown on the taximeter once the journey has been completed, and will be communicated by the taxi operator on the Bolt Platform. The fare in force is available for consultation by the passenger in the vehicle.

Hi [~accountid:6131df23dae0a20071abba9c] 

Gotcha! So when it comes to deleted accounts - we anonymize most of it, however we do retain order history, support tickets and some other data because either we’re obliged by law to keep it for certain time (e.g. tax / accounting) or in our interest, to for instance, defend ourselves in legal claims. 



If we need to open a safety tool on deleted account – it’s in our interest to investigate – we can analyze the orders or incidents on it. 



What the KB you share to refers to is that we currently have no way of restoration of deleted profiles – in other words, we do not “resurrect” deleted profiles. Once a profile is deleted it is deleted forever. The data we retain on deleted profiles is only data that is strictly necessary for the purposes described in the first paragraph of this answer. This data, however, is no longer matched to a particular user. In this case, you cannot reach out to the deleted account owner, because we no longer retain this data. 



If you were planning to open safety tool and communicate any data / events from that deleted account to the person who contacted us, we’d need to identify that they were the rightful owner of the deleted account. Otherwise we cannot share any information about the deleted account with the person who contacted us. There is [account details history|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/identity/consumers/rider/72542180/history?tz=Europe%2FTallinn&filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%7D%7D], or [log in history|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/identity/consumers/rider/72542180/history?tz=Europe%2FTallinn&filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%7D%7D] for instance - you may ask the person who contacted you to send you phone bill for number ending with 6959 - which was the number used for all log ins.



I hope this answers your issue. If not, let me know. Always happy to help.

[~accountid:6215e9f275803500683497d5] offered some insight:
I noticed that there is "+5V" line which you have meant common for all sensors.
To clarify this, then each sensor has a separate +5V output. This is to pinpoint the exact failed sensor in case it fails. If the supply line is common, then it is not possible to pinpoint the exact component and on Cobras this lead to a situation, when a lot of components could be thrown away due to bad diagnosing by mechanics.
I also marked them on the picture to make it more clear what I mean.
Also, I would like to propose that maybe it would make sense to use only 3 connectors from controller to the "upper" part of the bike instead of 4.
Cables "4" and "5" on drawing "splitter-based wires var 3" could be combined into single cable and number 2 cable could stay as is. This way, all the "sensor and light stuff" would be in 1 cable and all the "IoT stuff" would be in another cable.
This is similar approach as used on D1.
In addition to this there would be a cable from battery to controller from the "upper" part of the ebike.
The cable diameter connecting to 15 pin connector is 6mm and the cable diameter to 6 pin connector is 4mm on D1. I have also added pictures of the connectors we use on D1 for reference.Regarding the battery and motor connectors on controller, they are still open unfortunately because Genfo used connectors with incorrect rating.

_- TUPE transfer is when there's either:_

* _a business transfer_
* _a service provider change_

_A business transfer is when an organisation, or part of it, is transferred from one employer to another._

_A service provider change is when a service is transferred to a new provider. For example, when another company takes over a contract for office cleaning etc_ 

* _TUPE stands for 'Transfer of Undertakings (Protection of Employment) Regulations 2006' and its amendment in 2014. Meaning that the employee transferring to you cannot be worse off to what the employee was in their previous employment._ 

2. On the basis of the above, have we confirmed that TUPE definitely applies in this instance? The Council has said ‘TUPE may apply’.

# What does TUPE mean in practice? Do we need to keep all employees? Is there a certain period of time they must be retained before redundancies can be considered?
_It depends on the contract and agreement but there are options to put employees who TUPIED over at risk of redundancy. You will find that most of the time the Council will try and ask you to retain all employees or as many as possible. Its common practice in the UK that the Council tenders various services such cleaning etc and its only operator who changes and employees TUPE over._ 
# What are the mandatory redundancy requirements in the UK (ie. number of weeks per months of service)?

_If the new employer makes redundancies after a TUPE transfer, they're responsible for redundancy pay._
_The new and old employer can agree to include redundancy costs in the sale._

*Working out redundancy pay*

_An employee's length of service is protected in a TUPE transfer. This means their redundancy pay is based on how long they worked for both the old and new employer._

_In a TUPE transfer, employees who transfer keep their terms and conditions of employment. This might include enhanced redundancy pay. Enhanced means more than the legal minimum amount._

_To find out what costs exactly are we talking about we must check the following:_ 

* _employees' contracts_
* _company policies_
* _any collective agreements between employees and a trade union_

*If the employee have a statutory redundancy pay- yet to be determined* 

The maximum statutory pay for a week is £700.
CALCULATIONS : 
1 and a half week's pay for each full year they were aged 41 years or older

1 week's pay for each full year they were aged 22 or older, but aged under 41

half a week's pay for each full year they were aged under 22

+ their notice period 

*Also there has to be rationale for the redundancy* *_after the transfer_*
_After employees transfer, employers can only make redundancies related to the transfer if there is both:_

* _a genuine redundancy situation_
* _an 'economic, technical or organisational' (ETO) reason involving a change in the workforce_

_A genuine redundancy situation could be where part, or all, of the organisation is:_

* _closing, or has already closed_
* _changing the types or number of roles needed to do certain work_
* _changing location_

_Economic, technical or organisational (ETO) reasons_ 

_ETO reasons include:_

* _economic reasons – for example, essential cost-saving requirements_
* _technical reasons – for example, using new processes or equipment_
* _organisational reasons – for example, making changes to the structure of an organistion_

_ETO reasons must involve a change in the workforce. This could include:_

* _redundancies_
* _a significant restructure_
* _a change in location of the workplace_

_If an employer makes an employee redundant without a valid ETO reason, it will be an_ *_automatic unfair dismissal. (capped at_*  *£115,115 )*

_In this situation, the employee could make a claim to an employment tribunal. To make a claim they must have been employed continuously by the employer for 2 years or more._

*Dear all, here is an update on this file - DEADLINE 16 April 2025* 

On 17th January we received the decision of the AMT regarding the administrative complaint submitted by Bolt on 28 August 2024. [^Oficio nº 00267_16JAN_PLMJ_Bolt (1).pdf] 

In the decision, the AMT has reinforced its Opinion No. 37/AMT/2024, which determined that the provision of taxi transport services via an electronic platform under the contractual taxi fare model (Tariff C) is not legally compliant. 

*i.            Legal Grounds for the Decision*

* +Regulatory & Competitive Concerns:+ While the model aligns with contractual tariff requirements, its +pricing structure and geographical flexibility+ create potential +market distortions+, allowing taxi operators on the platform to circumvent standard taxi fare regulations and restrictions applicable to non-platform taxis.  Additionally, the AMT maintains that Tariff C should not be used as a generalised alternative to metered fares.
* +Non-Compliance with the Legal Framework+: The AMT affirms the model +conflicts with Article 22(3) of Decree-Law No. 101/2023 and Article 2(4) of Law No. 45/2018+, as it enables services that resemble TVDE operations without adhering to the corresponding regulatory framework.
* +Lack of Effective Oversight+: The AMT affirms Bolt has not provided sufficient mechanisms to +supervise compliance+ with municipal taxi quotas, nor has it demonstrated an +effective allocation system+ to prevent taxis from operating outside their licensed geographic areas.
* +*Pending Regulatory Developments*+*: The* +*new AMT Tariff Regulation*+ *will explicitly govern fixed-price digital taxi bookings, and the AMT considers that Bolt should await its publication before implementing this pricing model.*

*ii.           Potential Options going forward*

* +Await for the publication of the new Tariff Regulation of the AMT to make available a fixed amount by ride (not taximeter) as suggested by the regulator:+ 
** This option is beneficial from a cost and PR point of view
** The negative side is that the deployment of the tariff is depended on the prior approval of the AMT (eg regarding financials)
* +Lodge a Judicial appeal+
** Should Bolt wish to challenge this decision in court, the deadline to file an appeal is *16 April 2025* (3 months deadline, as per article 58, no. 1 paragraph a) of the PT Administrative Procedural Code).
** Strategically, a potential advantage of filing a lawsuit would be stress Bolt’s position of principle in courts and, separately, engage with AMT again to attempt a balance of positions.
** However, +this option has material shortcomings as we noted already in the past (no suspensive effect, years for a final decision, costs with outside attorney and the tribunal, effect on the relation with the regulator)+..
** Potential Legal Grounds for a Judicial Appeal would be:
*** +Misalignment with the AMT’s Own Regulatory Framework:+ The AMT contends that the contractual taxi fare model infringes regulatory and competitive principles, citing issues with geographic contingencies and alleged market distortions. However, the AMT has not provided sufficient evidence to substantiate claims of abuse or regulatory non-compliance under Tariff C. Additionally, Bolt has demonstrated its commitment to ensuring compliance with geographic contingencies, including the development of in-app solutions to address potential gaps. Providing the AMT with examples of these in-app measures could effectively counter their assertions.
*** +Inconsistencies with the Draft Tariff Regulation+: The Draft Tariff Regulation, specifically Article 12, explicitly permits three pricing models, including Tariff C. This suggests that the AMT’s current enforcement action against Tariff C is at odds with its own forthcoming regulatory framework
*** +Economic and Financial Recovery Principles+: The AMT’s concerns regarding Tariff C are that it allegedly hinders the economic and financial recovery principles outlined in Article 20, no. 1, of Decree-Law No. 101/2023. Bolt’s argument shall focus on the fact that the Tariff C fare model provides a balance between operational cost recovery and passenger affordability, which was not initially used in the administrative complaint.
*** +Role of Bolt in Pricing Determination+: Contrary to the AMT’s assertions, Bolt does not unilaterally determine the final price for trips under the Tariff C model. It should be reinforced (as stated in the administrative complaint) that for metered fares, Bolt only provides an estimated price range as a reference, which is non-binding, and that the final price is determined by the taximeter.

We write in relation to your data subject rights request, which we received on 27 December 2024. Please find our response below.

*(1) Copy of your personal data*

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties. Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

We therefore attach copies of your personal data to which you are entitled. 

*(2) Information regarding the irregular activity detected on your account*

As noted in previous messages with you, your voucher was excluded from the calculation as our system detected irregular activity on your account. We are unable to share any further information on such irregular activity, as to share confidential information in this regard could allow third parties to circumvent Bolt’s irregular activity detection and prevention processes, which in turn would undermine the equitable management of the Bolt platform and threaten the rights and freedoms of other Bolt users. We apologise for any inconvenience caused.

*(3) Your rights*

You have the right to request rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing of personal data concerning you or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You have the right to complain directly to the appropriate supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy. 

If you have any additional questions, please let us know.

Yours sincerely,

*Bolt*

The user is reporting a double-charge because of incremental authorization.
Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. This typically happens in scenarios where the final amount of the transaction is not known upfront or may change.

I have checked the case and everything looks good on Bolt’s end. The pre-authorization has been released to the customer. 
You can ask the customer to reach out to their bank in order to confirm the authorized funds have been released. Their bank can locate the funds with the authorization date and amount.

Our liability in such accident caused by a brake malfunction is complex and depends on several factors. Our terms and conditions generally are placing a) responsibility on the rider for safety checks and proper use. However, b) we could be held liable if the malfunction was due to our negligence in maintenance or a manufacturing defect we should have been aware of.However, this would additionally mean that we would need to prove that we did everything correct and that the rider was being negligent for not checking the brakes. But in all honestly I doubt that a Court would take our side in this situation.
